subject: PulseChat: real-time response slowdown — immediate actions & canary roll
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@pulsechat.io>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@pulsechat.io
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: [PulseChat] Sudden response slowdowns on /v1/chat/stream

Hi team,

We're seeing intermittent high tail latency (~2.5-4s) for streaming tokens on our US region chat traffic starting ~08:30 PT. It looks concentrated on mid-length conversations (200-700 tokens) and affects about 12% of sessions right now. No code deploys on our side during that time.

Impact: degraded user typing experience; we have a few paid customers who reported frustration.

Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation on Redwood's side and any immediate mitigations we should apply? We've already tried switching to a slightly smaller model variant and saw no material change.

Attaching a small telemetry dump.

Thanks,
Daniel
Ops Lead, PulseChat

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:34:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: [PulseChat] Sudden response slowdowns on /v1/chat/stream

Daniel —

Thanks for the heads up and for the telemetry. We're seeing the same elevated p95/p99 for streaming responses in our US-west fleet starting ~08:15 PT; engineering is triaging now. Quick items to try while we investigate:

- Short-term client-side mitigations (low friction):
  * Reduce requested max_tokens to 512 for sessions with heavy history; that narrows batch size variance.
  * If you use streaming, enable smaller chunk_size (e.g., 64 tokens) to reduce perceived stall windows.
  * Retry-on-partial: if your client sees >3s gap between chunks, attempt a single reconnect with the same session id.

- Server-side suggestions we are attempting:
  * Canary roll a routing tweak to prefer lower-latency edge shards for live traffic (5–10% initially).
  * Temporarily relax batching on the affected shard class to prioritize latency over throughput.

I'll keep you updated as we have more from infra. I've created an incident record and added Marissa (CS) and Vivek (SRE) to the thread for coordination.

Soojin
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:07:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: [PulseChat] Sudden response slowdowns on /v1/chat/stream

Quick engineering update and temporary playbook:

Root cause (preliminary):
- At ~08:10 PT a subset of edge-router instances in us-west transitioned to a new batching kernel configuration during routine autoscaling. The kernel had an edge-case where mix of mid-length contexts + prefix caching created unusually large internal batch windows for streaming paths. This increased token emission latency for affected shards.

Mitigations applied (now):
- Rolled back the kernel change for the affected instance set at 10:42 PT.
- Forced canary routing to route 15% of PulseChat traffic to the unaffected shard pool (canary id: canary-742).
- Temporarily disabled aggressive continuous batching on streaming endpoints for the impacted shard class.

Recommended customer actions (what we suggest you do now):
1) If possible, enable client reconnect-on-gap policy (single reconnect, preserve session id).
2) Lower chunk_size to 48–64 tokens for streaming sessions until we finish verification.
3) If your workload is latency-sensitive, temporarily reroute high-value customers to the alternate region (us-east) — we can assist with edge routing config.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll monitor for 6 hours and revert canary routing in 1–2 hours if metrics look good.
- Postmortem with timeline, telemetry, and long-term fix (kernel safeguards + extended unit tests) will be published in 72 hours.

I'll post a short status update at 13:00 PT. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your user experience.

— Vivek
SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: PulseChat incident follow-up: remediation summary and next steps

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for quick reporting and for working with the on-call team. Summary and customer-facing follow-up below:

What happened (short):
- A batching-kernel configuration change coupled with autoscaling resulted in increased batch windows on a subset of streaming shards in us-west, causing elevated client-visible token latency for ~12% of sessions between 08:15–10:45 PT on Apr 14.

What we did:
- Rolled back the change at 10:42 PT; applied a conservative routing canary and disabled aggressive continuous batching for streaming on impacted shards.
- Monitored and validated user-perceived latencies returned to baseline within ~30–45 minutes after rollback.
- Identified longer-term fixes: kernel validation tests, improved rollout gating, and additional telemetry for per-session emit-delays.

Customer impact:
- You reported degraded UX for a subset of sessions. We observed increased p95/p99 for streaming chunk emit times, consistent with your telemetry.

Short-term actions for PulseChat (our recommended checklist):
- Keep client reconnect-on-gap enabled for 72 hours.
- Use chunk_size <= 64 for streaming sessions while we complete verification.
- If you'd like, we can shift high-value customers to us-east for 24 hours — let me know and we'll coordinate with your ops team.

Compensation and next steps: 
- We're offering a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of April 2027 usage for affected production tokens under DEAL-7893. This is a credit offer; your account team (Marissa) will follow up with formal billing adjustment.
- A full postmortem is being drafted and will be shared via the linked Drive doc within 72 hours: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/pulsechat-incident-20270414

I'll keep this thread open until you've confirmed the customer-facing mitigation is sufficient. If you'd prefer a quick 30-minute sync with product and SRE, we can schedule one this week.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
